_comment: Single source of truth for the Content-Security-Policy. vercel.json serves it and scripts/verify-csp.mjs proves it in a real browser; the script fails if the two drift. expectedBlocked documents anything the policy is meant to block on purpose - it is empty because nothing currently should be, and it is kept empty on purpose: an entry here silences a violation, so leaving a resolved one in place would hide the same tracker if it ever returned. Three advertising endpoints have appeared so far and ALL THREE were fixed at the source rather than allowlisted. (1) A GTM-injected Meta Pixel, 2026-08-06, setting an _fbp cookie before consent; the tag was removed from the container. (2) GA4 conversion pings to pagead2.googlesyndication.com carrying the page URL, the page title and a gacid client identifier, attempted even with the consent signal denied (gcs=G100, npa=1). Cause: a GA4-to-Google-Ads link to account Digitizer 299-357-1794 created 2026-08-06. Disabling Personalized Advertising did NOT stop them; deleting the link did, and all 15 pages went silent. Time elapsed between the two changes, so this does not strictly isolate which one mattered - but the endpoint is conversion measurement, which belongs to the link rather than to personalisation. (3) Microsoft Clarity, allowed here for session recording, redirected c.clarity.ms/c.gif to c.bing.com/c.gif with a CtsSyncId that changed on every page load - an identity sync into Microsoft's advertising graph, on all 14 pages, before consent. c.bing.com was NOT added to img-src. Fixed at the source by turning the Cookies toggle OFF in Clarity's project settings (Settings > Setup > Advanced settings), which enables Clarity Consent Mode; the site then passes ad_Storage: denied unconditionally via consentv2. Measured after the change: zero violations across all 14 pages, so no expectedBlocked entry was needed. Note Consent Mode is off by default outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, so this is a setting someone must keep on, not a default that protects itself. Clarity was later removed entirely and replaced by PostHog, so its allowances are gone from the policy - but the c.bing.com finding is kept on record here because the endpoint is still absent by decision, and scripts/verify-consent.mjs still fails on it. If any of these ever reappear, the CSP will turn the gate red again, which is the intended behaviour. On PostHog: everything reaches it through t.benkalsky.co.il, a first-party reverse proxy, so one host covers the script, the recorder and ingestion. worker-src was NOT added: the recorder does construct workers from data: and blob: URLs, but both were measured as ALLOWED under this policy without a worker-src entry, so adding one would have been a widening nobody needed - which is what the previous PostHog branch assumed.
policy: default-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://www.googletagmanager.com https://t.benkalsky.co.il; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https://www.googletagmanager.com https://*.google-analytics.com https://*.googletagmanager.com; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://*.google-analytics.com https://*.googletagmanager.com https://*.analytics.google.com https://t.benkalsky.co.il; frame-src https://www.googletagmanager.com; manifest-src 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests; report-uri /api/csp-report/; report-to csp
